svg.title: Controlled record correction
svg.desc: Course 1 Module 6 Lesson 6.1 visual explaining that cultivation record corrections must follow the governing record system and facility procedure, preserve the original information or audit trail, show attribution and timing, and never silently overwrite, erase, backdate, or invent missing data. A paper correction example is shown only as conditional when the governing procedure permits it.

g.text: THC ACADEMY • COURSE 1 • MODULE 6
Controlled Record Correction
Lesson 6.1
Technician I foundation
The governing record system and facility procedure determine the correction method.
Every correction should preserve history
✓ Keep the original information or audit trail
✓ Show the corrected value or status clearly
✓ Preserve who made the change
✓ Preserve when the change was made
✓ Include a reason when the procedure requires it
✓ Keep missing information visibly missing
Goal: another qualified person can reconstruct
what was entered, what changed, by whom and when.
Paper record example — only if permitted
The governing procedure may require a specific correction
method such as keeping the original entry legible, adding
the corrected information, attribution, date/time and reason.
Do not assume one paper method applies everywhere.
Never manufacture a clean-looking history
✕ Silent overwrite or erased original
✕ Backdating a late entry
✕ Replacing missing data with a target or guess
✕ Unattributed changes or uncontrolled shared identity
Paper and digital corrections are system-controlled.
Preserve the original information or audit trail; do not invent, erase or silently rewrite history.
